keyFindings.description: settleEndedHolds reads its fence only after the hand-back loop, so an abandoned role move still writes shared state. Sequence: move A awaits client.unsubscribe at :2227; A's deadline fires and roleMoves starts the next task; a session event lands and rebind (:2536) runs endUnwantedRoleNow, which inserts a hand-back at :2017; a JS Map iterator visits entries added during iteration, so A's loop visits the new entry, deletes it at :2219 and - when A's `wanted` is that role, the ordinary heartbeat case - takes the restore branch at :2220-2225, overwriting claimedRoleTopic/claimedRoleSessionID/holdUnconfirmed that the replacing move settled. The next pass then sees held !== desired and hands the role back through endRole(), closing every subject a plugin opened whileHolding, which the code itself (:2358-2361) says only that plugin reopens. A second loss on the same path: an entry A deleted whose unsubscribe failed goes into `failed`, and the post-loop `if (!live()) return false` at :2240 drops it from both pendingHandBacks and abandonedHolds, so the hold is leaked with nothing left to settle it. This contradicts the PR body's claim that an abandoned task 'cannot record a role claim the listener has since given elsewhere'. Fix: read live() at the top of each iteration, before the delete at :2219.

setEnvoyRole checks its fence after client.setRole resolves and then throws AbandonedTaskError saying 'nothing was recorded', while the listener has accepted the claim. The adjacent !sessionOpen(id) branch (:1905-1921) handles the same situation correctly by keeping the hold under the id the listener named so the next pass converges it; the abandoned branch keeps nothing. Result: the listener names a live, heartbeating session as the holder of a role that session's heldRole() does not know about, so no pass ever hands it back and the listener never reaps it (the session keeps heartbeating). A later claim of another role does not end it either, since previousTopic is undefined at :1939. Messages published to that role topic go to a session that refuses them (subscribeLegionNotice 'does not hold role'), for the life of the process. envoy.test.ts 'a task that answers after its deadline writes nothing over what a newer one settled' pins the leak as correct behaviour ('The listener did hear the abandoned claim; this process recorded nothing of it'). Fix: record the landed claim as a hand-back (pendingHandBacks, as :2017 does) before throwing, and change that test to assert the hand-back.

An explicit ENVOY_PASS_DEADLINE_MS is used as given (floored only at MIN_INTERVAL_MS); only the fallback is max(heartbeatMs, 30 s). With a value below heartbeatMs - envoy-settings.test.ts:103 pins ENVOY_PASS_DEADLINE_MS=7500 against a 100 s heartbeat as valid - every pass is abandoned before the next tick, so healing is false at every tick and the heartbeat backstop at envoy.ts:1729-1742, which lives inside the `if (healing)` branch, never fires. A pass that wedges in its inbound-open section (ensureConnection/subscribe/watchAgentStream/recoverRegisteredInterests, envoy.ts:2145-2169, all awaited before registerSession) then never reaches a registration, nothing else posts one, and the record lapses - the behaviour this change exists to stop. The pane is meanwhile told 'the session registration is being refreshed on its own, and recovers once the pass settles' (:1720-1723), which is false in that configuration. Fix: floor the resolved passDeadlineMs at heartbeatMs (one line), which also makes DEFAULT_PASS_DEADLINE_MS a true floor.

The stated guarantee 'two whole refreshes may fail before a live pane is dropped' is not delivered at the shipped numbers, and it is repeated in packages/envoy-client/CHANGELOG.md, the PR body's Change list and .github/scripts/check-heartbeat-margin.sh:14-17 (whose rule 1 is `3 x heartbeat <= lifetime`, today 300000 == 300000 exactly). The record expires 300 s after the listener accepted a write; the third refresh after two failures is only attempted 3 x 100 s after the first was attempted and still needs its round trip, and setInterval never fires early. The tester's own measured healthy gaps between accepted registrations (100.4, 99.9, 99.8, 100.3, 99.7, 99.8 s) give consecutive triples of 300.1, 300.0, 299.8, 299.8 s, straddling the lifetime. What the numbers deliver is one failed refresh, as 120 s did. Fix: state one failed refresh everywhere, or give the rule real slack (a lower DEFAULT_HEARTBEAT_MS, or a strict `<` with a round-trip allowance).

The plugin heartbeat moved to 100 s in liveness.go but three sibling copies of the old number were left: pluginHeartbeat = 2 * time.Minute with the comment 'the plugin heartbeats every pluginHeartbeat' (notice_exceptions.go:32,37, used as the second re-hold delay at :51), 'The plugin heartbeats every 2 minutes, so this allows two missed heartbeats' (packages/envoy/internal/session/claim.go:10-11; at 100 s the 5-minute window allows three), and the same sentence in packages/envoy/cmd/listener/delivery.go:301. Behaviour is unchanged, the statements are now false, and the new required check reads only liveness.go, so the drift it advertises catching is already in the tree at merge.

ensureConnection assigns the shared `connection` at :882 with no fence; reconcileNow reads live() only after it returns (:2147-2150). A pass abandoned during its dial whose dial later resolves overwrites the connection a newer pass established; the newer object is then unreferenced and never drained by cleanup (:2602 drains only `connection`), and maxReconnectAttempts: -1 keeps it alive. Narrow - nats.js bounds the dial at its 20 s default, well inside the 100 s deadline - but it is the one shared-state write the fence docblock's 'every continuation that could write shared state checks it' (:167-170) misses.

The worst case is computed as heartbeat + max(heartbeat, pass_deadline) + call_budget and attributed to 'a refresh held behind a serial-queue task abandoned at its deadline', but the backstop at envoy.ts:1729-1742 posts the refresh at the first tick where healing and the registration is a whole interval old, whatever passDeadlineMs is, so the real bound is 2 x heartbeat + call_budget. The two coincide only because max(100000, 30000) happens to equal the heartbeat. Raising DEFAULT_PASS_DEADLINE_MS to 200000 would fail CI (310250 > 300000) and tell the author to raise the registry TTL, while production stays bounded at 210250 ms.

The smoke hardcodes record_lifetime_s=300 and default_heartbeat_ms=100000, the two numbers the new check exists to de-duplicate ('It keeps no copy of any of these numbers', check-heartbeat-margin.sh:43-45), and the check does not parse the smoke. When DEFAULT_HEARTBEAT_MS next moves, CI stays green and the smoke measures against the old budget.

thermonuclear.adjudication: Four findings carried (the two fence holes, the pass-deadline floor, the margin claim). Rejected: the quality pair's remedy of deleting Fence/AbandonedTaskError/the deadline entirely - spec acceptance 1 asks for the stall to be bounded, the architect accepted that design, and the deadline is what keeps a wedged task from holding session events and Legion claim calls behind it. Deferred to the fast-follow: the serialQueue extraction and the smoke's copied constants. Not carried: DEFAULT_PASS_DEADLINE_MS naming (folded into the floor fix).
